notes: Segment covers Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa in full per SCHEMA/MINISTRIES ownership rules. Key verified 2025-26 changes: Maharashtra Governor changed to Jishnu Dev Varma (10 Mar 2026); Deputy CM Ajit Pawar died in an air-charter crash 28 Jan 2026 and was succeeded as Deputy CM by his wife Sunetra Pawar (31 Jan 2026), who also became NCP national president (26 Feb 2026) — corroborated independently on both the Ajit Pawar and Sunetra Pawar Wikipedia pages, flagged here given its unusual and high-impact nature. Goa Governor changed to Ashok Gajapathi Raju (26 Jul 2025). Gujarat Governor Acharya Devvrat's tenure (since 2019) could not be independently reconfirmed against a 2025-26 source; flagged medium confidence in case of an unreported transfer. Gujarat gained a Deputy CM (Harsh Sanghavi, 17 Oct 2025) and a new district, Vav-Tharad (2 Oct 2025, carved from Banaskantha), raising its district count to 34. Maharashtra minister Dhananjay Munde resigned from the cabinet (Food & Civil Supplies) on 4 March 2025 amid the Beed sarpanch-murder political fallout, confirmed via Wikipedia; he is correctly omitted from the active minister list. (A later reshuffle around 20 May 2025 is when Chhagan Bhujbal is understood to have taken over the Food & Civil Supplies portfolio.) GAPS / lower-confidence areas: (1) Individual Wikipedia URLs were verified only for top office-holders (Governors, CMs, Deputy CMs, Speakers, a few others) — not for the ~50 rank-and-file cabinet/MoS ministers, to avoid inventing unverified links; a follow-up pass should add these. (2) Chief Secretary appointment dates for Gujarat and Goa, MPSC/GPSC/Goa PSC chair appointment dates, and Goa's DGP name could not be confirmed from available sources. (3) Maharashtra, Gujarat and Goa State Human Rights Commission chair tenures are low confidence (thin sourcing). (4) Mayors were resolved only for Panaji (Goa's single municipal corporation); Mumbai's BMC and other Maharashtra/Gujarat corporations have had no elected mayor/corporators since their last councils' terms expired (elections repeatedly postponed) — administrator rule — so no mayor holder was recorded for them; this should be confirmed and made explicit per corporation in a follow-up pass. (5) Maharashtra Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council and LoP-in-Council are thinly sourced. (6) WebSearch was unavailable for this run (session budget exhausted); all research used WebFetch against Wikipedia pages plus stable general knowledge for uncontested figures (seat counts, etc.) — a follow-up pass should cross-check against PIB/official state portals per the schema's preferred-source order.
